writeup: TIC 188629001 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 2.86% occurring every 0.7256 days, producing a strong detection signal with a signal-to-noise ratio of 123.2 in the transit search algorithm. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the eclipse signature at the target location, with a centroid offset of 2.8 arcsec and a peak signal-to-noise of 18.9 in difference imaging. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. All data quality checks passed without issues.
